name: Anti-wrinkle pillow

lead: Anti-wrinkle pillows are contoured, cushioned or pillowcase-style products meant to reduce facial compression during sleep, which is thought to contribute to sleep lines on the forehead, cheeks and chest.
The idea is plausible because sleep wrinkles are linked to repeated pressure, but there are no good trials of these products. Sleeping on the back avoids facial contact without any product.

paras: They try to limit facial compression and shear, for example with cut-outs or pillows that cradle the head, while silk or copper-infused covers aim at reducing friction.

Risk is low; discomfort and poorer sleep from an awkward shape are the main reported downsides. Product claims are weakly supported and much of the supporting material is from marketing. Sun exposure, collagen loss and aging are described as larger drivers of wrinkles.
